post.instagram_caption:
The Nasdaq just had its worst day since April 2025: down 5.5% in one session.

The Nasdaq fell 5.52% to 24,315 on Thursday, November 5, its worst day since April 2025, and closed in a correction, more than 10% below its record. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% and the Dow lost 1,833 points, one day after the Dow jumped 1,569 points following the US midterms. Chip stocks led the drop: the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 12.25%, AMD 17.3% and Nvidia 9.3%. Yahoo Finance reports that Democrats' sweep of Congress raised concerns about regulatory hurdles for AI data center buildouts, and Nomura's Charlie McElligott described a hedge fund rush to protect profits before year end. Figures as of the November 5, 2026 close.
